requirement: In Markdown, escaped roles and role-looking text in inline code, fenced code, or raw HTML MUST remain literal and MUST NOT count as references. Raw HTML means an HTML block, an HTML comment, or an inline HTML tag including its attributes; text between inline tags is ordinary Markdown. A `{req}` directive inside a fenced code example and a legacy inline `{req}` role MUST NOT define a requirement.
rationale: **Verdict:** the sources satisfy `requirements.references.markdown_literals`. I found no unacknowledged gaps that change this, and a few minor test omissions that I judge acceptable. ## Implementation All obligations are carried by the `{impl}`-marked code in `src/lib.rs`. That code is the only place Markdown roles and directives are recognised. Every consumer goes through it: book rendering, evidence validation, authoring inputs, term dependencies and the index. - **Escaped roles.** `reference_roles` skips any `{` for which `is_escaped` is true. `is_escaped` counts the backslashes before the `{` and treats an odd count as an escape, so `\{impl}` is literal and `\\{impl}` is not. - **Inline code, fenced code and raw HTML.** `protected_ranges` runs pulldown-cmark over the content and protects the ranges of `Start(CodeBlock)`, `Code`, `Html` and `InlineHtml` events. `reference_roles` skips roles inside those ranges via `is_protected`. This matches the stated definition of raw HTML: - `Html` covers HTML blocks. - `InlineHtml` covers inline tags with their attributes, and inline comments. - Text between inline tags such as `…` is not protected, so it counts as ordinary Markdown. - **`{req}` directive inside fenced code.** `definition_blocks` collects the code-block ranges first. It rejects any opening fence line that overlaps one (`overlaps_protected`), and ignores closing-fence candidates inside code. - **Legacy inline `{req}` role.** Definitions come only from colon-fence parsing in `definition_blocks`. No path treats `` {req}`x` `` as a definition, and `reference_roles` recognises only impl/cite/test/term. - **Scope.** `markdown=false` leaves the protection ranges empty. This is exercised by `roles_in_raw_html_stay_literal` and keeps Rust-comment scanning unaffected. The helpers (`overlaps_protected`, `protected_ranges`, `is_protected`, `is_escaped`) and the two main functions all carry `{impl}` markers for this requirement. I found no unmarked code that implements part of it. ## Tests All tests carry `{test}` markers. - `code_examples_and_legacy_roles_remain_literal` covers inline code, a `:::{req}` directive inside a fenced block (with indentation), the legacy `{req}` role staying literal, and a real directive still rendering. - `markdown_examples_and_escaped_references_stay_literal` runs through `preprocess_book` with an inline-code role, a fenced-code role and a backslash-escaped role. All three stay literal and none is rendered as a badge. - `roles_in_raw_html_stay_literal` covers an HTML block, a block-level comment, an inline comment, a role inside an attribute value, and text between inline tags. It asserts that only the between-tags role is a reference, and that `markdown=false` does not protect HTML. - `colon_directives_render_markdown_bodies_and_legacy_roles_stay_literal` covers the legacy `{req}` role not defining a requirement, alongside a real directive whose body contains a fenced block. - `references_in_requirement_bodies_are_scanned_as_markdown` checks a fenced example inside a requirement body. - `source_references_are_covered_by_evidence_inputs` (`src/evidence.rs`) checks that inline-code and fenced-code roles in `.md` files are not collected as references, so they cause no "no matching requirement" errors. - `examples_are_distinct_definitions_and_tests_link_to_them` also asserts that a fenced `:::{example}` defines nothing. ## Minor observations I did not treat these as gaps. - No test has two backslashes before a role, although the parity logic is simple. - `Tag::CodeBlock` also protects indented code blocks, which is a reasonable reading of "code". - `is_escaped` also applies when `markdown=false`.
